title: U.S. House · New Jersey's 1st Congressional District
area: Camden County and parts of Gloucester and Burlington counties in South Jersey, including Camden, Cherry Hill, Gloucester Township, Sicklerville, and Williamstown.

context.text: Incumbent Donald Norcross ran unopposed in the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary, winning 100% of the vote (66,059 votes). Damon Galdo won the Republican primary unopposed with 100% of the vote (16,265 votes).

Cook Political Report rated the district's Partisan Voter Index as D+10 as of September 2026; Kamala Harris won the district 58.6%–39.9% under the current district lines in the 2024 presidential election.

candidates.name: Donald Norcross
candidates.ballotNote: Ran unopposed in the June 2 Democratic primary
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for New Jersey's 1st Congressional District (since 2014)

summary.text: Donald Norcross is the Democratic incumbent U.S. Representative for New Jersey's 1st District, in office since a November 2014 special election. An electrician by trade, he rose through the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers and served as president of the Southern New Jersey AFL-CIO before serving in the New Jersey Assembly and State Senate. He sits on the House Education and Workforce and Armed Services Committees and ran unopposed in the 2026 Democratic primary.

background.text: Born December 13, 1958, in Camden, New Jersey, and grew up in Pennsauken Township, according to Wikipedia; his House biography says he was born and raised in South Jersey.
Attended Camden County College and Rutgers University-Camden; Wikipedia lists an associate degree in criminal justice from Camden County College.
Trained as an electrician through a registered apprenticeship program and, according to his House biography, rose to become a business agent for IBEW Local 351.
Served as president of the Southern New Jersey AFL-CIO, which his House biography says he did for nearly 20 years.
Elected to the New Jersey General Assembly in 2009; appointed to fill a vacancy in the New Jersey Senate in 2010 and served there until his election to the U.S. House in 2014.
Won the Democratic primary and then both a special election to fill the remainder of Rob Andrews's term and the regular election in November 2014; he was sworn in on November 12, 2014.
Serves on the House Committee on Education and Workforce and the House Armed Services Committee, where his House biography says he is ranking member of the Tactical Air and Land Forces Subcommittee.

According to his House biography, he co-founded the Labor Caucus and the bipartisan Building Trades Caucus and introduced the No Tax Breaks for Union Busting Act, the Warehouse Worker Protection Act, and the Parity Enforcement Act.
A lifelong Camden County resident who, according to his House biography, lives with his wife Andrea; they have three adult children and four grandchildren.

positions.summary: WHYY reports he lists protecting access to reproductive health care as a priority and called the Supreme Court decision overturning Roe v. Wade "disgraceful."
Said in a statement that he opposes broad tariffs, as quoted by WHYY in 2026.
positions.quote: broad reckless tariffs that act as a tax on the working class and destabilize our supply chains

positions.summary: His official site lists investment in clean energy, including offshore wind and solar, as part of addressing climate change.
positions.quote: This responsibility also presents opportunities to create jobs and grow our economy by inventing in, manufacturing, and installing clean energy technology and other sustainable solutions here in South Jersey, including offshore wind and solar.

positions.summary: His official budget page calls for boosting tax revenue by ensuring the wealthiest pay their fair share.
positions.quote: We need to address the national debt by cutting wasteful spending, boosting tax revenue by ensuring the wealthiest pay their fair share, and investing in programs that promote economic growth and create family-sustaining jobs.

record.text: Sits on the House Committee on Armed Services (Seapower and Projection Forces; Tactical Air and Land Forces subcommittees) and the Committee on Education and the Workforce for the 119th Congress (2025–2026).

In prior Congresses, introduced the Veterans Freedom of Healthcare Act, which would have expanded the Veterans Choice program to let veterans obtain care from local providers regardless of distance to a VA facility, and the WORC Grant Program Act, which would have created competitive federal grants for manufacturing-worker scholarships.

Says he supported the bipartisan Denying Firearms and Explosives to Dangerous Terrorists Act, which would bar individuals on the federal Terrorist Watchlist from legally purchasing firearms, and served on the House Gun Violence Prevention Task Force.

candidates.name: Damon Galdo
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2 Republican primary unopposed

summary.text: Damon Galdo is a construction superintendent and small-business owner from West Deptford, New Jersey, and the Republican nominee for NJ-1. He has not held elected office; he lost Republican primaries for the seat in 2022 and 2024 before winning the 2026 nomination unopposed. His campaign materials emphasize border security, inflation, parental rights, and free speech.

background.text: Born in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania; lives in West Deptford, New Jersey; graduated from La Salle College High School in 1999.

Career experience includes working as a carpenter foreman and construction superintendent; in a 2025 Ballotpedia survey he describes himself as a construction superintendent, small-business owner, husband, and father.

In 2022 the New Jersey Globe described him as a West Deptford resident and construction superintendent filing petitions for the Republican nomination; it quoted his campaign announcement describing himself as a union carpenter with no political background.
Lost the Republican primary for NJ-1 in 2022 (31.0% to Claire Gustafson) and again in 2024 (14.9%, finishing third of three candidates) before winning the nomination unopposed in 2026.
Signed the Americans for Tax Reform Taxpayer Protection Pledge in his 2024 campaign.

priorities.text: Says his top messages are bringing real-world working experience to Congress, restoring fiscal accountability and secure borders, and defending free speech, parental rights, and the Constitution.
priorities.quote: I'm a constrruction superintendent, small business owner, husband, and father who knows what it means to work hard and make payroll. I'm running to bring real world experience to Congress and to stand up for families who feel ignored by career polititions.

priorities.text: Says he is passionate about border security and enforcement of immigration law, election integrity, reducing federal spending to fight inflation, and protecting working families from rising costs.

positions.summary: Says he is passionate about keeping the border secure and enforcing immigration law; his 2024 platform called for reinstating the Remain in Mexico policy and ending sanctuary policies.
positions.quote: I will support ending DACA, DAPA, Catch-and-Release, and all other programs that facilitate illegal immigration and benefit illegal immigrants, and I will support rebuilding the wall.

candidates.researchNotes: A 2026 WHYY voter guide quotes him on the economy and Iran policy, but those quotes do not take a side on the listed issues; no campaign website was reachable. No further positions or statements added.

statements.quote: When I'm in Congress, I will propose and support legislation that will allow us to drill for oil, mine for coal, frack, and invest in nuclear energy research.
statements.context: On his 2024 campaign website, per Ballotpedia

researchNotes: Donald Norcross has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey and his official House website's Sponsored Legislation issue page is undated, so the bills listed in his record reflect legislation he has introduced in prior Congresses rather than confirmed 2025-2026 introductions; per the research brief his federal floor votes and FEC totals are added separately by script. Damon Galdo's priorities and positions come from his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey and his 2024 campaign website (no updated 2026 issues page was found). Donald Norcross's labor-union roles are taken from his House biography (IBEW Local 351), which differs from the local number and title listed on Ballotpedia.
